Marissa — thanks for the summary and the docs. Quick answers below: 

1) Monthly volumes: baseline today is ~30M tokens/month. We expect growth and could be ~45M in 6 months given our roadmap. Peak-day we see up to ~5M tokens on high-traffic launches. P95 daily rate roughly 1.8M tokens.

2) Budget target: we're aiming for around $60–$80 per 1M tokens (this is our preferred target range before considering a reserved capacity commitment). If reserved capacity gives material discounts, we can consider a commit.

3) Burst pattern: typical sustained requests are constant for API calls from 2000 active users; bursts occur for 5–20 minutes around product events (e.g., promo emails, feature flaps). During bursts we can spike up to ~3x baseline sustained RPS.

Procurement: we need a one-pager SOW and an initial quote to share with procurement this week. Also please include overage terms and expected latency SLA for the region (us-west).

Thanks — feel free to loop in SEs for the rate-limit specifics.

—Alex

Thanks — copied Alex, below is a concise summary you can include in the SOW/quote. I also updated the attached rate_limits_plan.xlsx with numbers.

Technical / quota recommendations:
- Baseline quota: allocate a per-account token quota that aligns with monthly expected usage; for 30–45M/mo we typically provision a sustained QPS equivalent to the P95 daily (~1.8M tokens/day ~= ~21 tokens/sec sustained average depending on token sizes). For practical API throttles we set request-based quotas (requests/min) plus a token budget.
- Burst allowance: default hosted accounts support a 2x sustained burst for up to 10 minutes without additional charge (soft burst). For this customer (3x bursts up to 20 mins) recommend: either (A) a committed burst window as a special config (allow 3x for 20 minutes, then soft throttle) or (B) reserved capacity (preferred) which eliminates burst overage risk.

Overage / pricing mechanics:
- On-demand unit price (example in sheet): $80 / 1M tokens.
- Overage billing for bursts: bursts beyond soft allowance are billed as overage at a 1.5x multiplier of the on-demand unit price (so $120 / 1M in this example) for the overage portion.
- Reserved capacity: for a 12-mo commit we can offer $45–$55 / 1M tokens depending on commit size and term (see sheet scenarios). Reserved capacity also provides higher guaranteed burst headroom and faster emergency quota increases.
- Emergency quota increases: standard SLA for hosted customers is 24–48 hours for quota increases; enterprise Reserved plans can get guaranteed 4–8 hour escalation paths (per SLA addendum).

Other notes:
- We support soft throttles (429 with Retry-After) and request-level traces so we can identify burst sources.
- Network/latency SLA for us-west: 99.9% availability target for Dedicated; hosted SLA available as add-on — include explicit latency targets in the SOW if required.

Next steps:
1) Marissa: include the on-demand and reserved pricing rows (I updated the sheet). Recommend presenting both: on-demand @ $80 / 1M with 1.5x overage, and reserved example @ $50 / 1M with committed burst headroom.
2) Alex: confirm if procurement needs a formal SLA addendum and expected signature timeline.
3) We can provision a short-term trial with a slightly higher soft burst allowance while procurement completes the SOW.

If you want, I can also draft a one-paragraph blurb for the SOW that spells out the overage formula and escalation steps.
